plan: With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, i.e., bid = value × 2/3. This balances the trade-off between winning probability and profit margin. My value is $48, so I'll bid approximately $32 to maximize expected profit while remaining competitive against Betty and Charles.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the standard first-price auction equilibrium bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3. This balances winning probability against overpaying. My value is $38, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 of that to maximize expected profit while still maintaining a good chance of winning against the other two bidders.

With value $12 and 3 bidders (n=3) drawing uniformly from $0-$49, the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n = 2/3 of my value, balancing win probability against profit margin. This gives a bid of approximately $8, which maximizes expected profit given the symmetric equilibrium strategy against similarly rational bidders.
